subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw support gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: Both options change a sensitive provider credential boundary, and automation should not decide whether node hosts may acquire or transfer gateway-owned OAuth material without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving loopback/tunnel setups.

options.title: Forward credentials to the gateway
options.body: Design an authenticated gateway RPC or setup flow that moves provider auth material to the gateway store without first consuming credentials locally.

options.title: Warn but keep permissive
options.body: Warn node-host users that login only affects the local node, accepting the existing wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving loopback/tunnel setups.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle authored the maintainer draft and verification path for the exact guard direction, making them the best available routing candidate for the credential-boundary decision.
